objects.original: Actual unit sphere S, literal inclusion iota, inclusion-induced tangent length and its C1 path-distance infimum.
objects.reconstructed: Norm-one subtype with the standard stereographic sphere atlas, N_z(v)=enorm(d i_z(v)), and the resulting riemannianEDist.
objects.evidence: The source four definitions, compiler ARG_6 through ARG_9, and module lines 203-207 fix the actual sphere, atlas and inclusion ENorm. There is no arbitrary norm hypothesis.

domains.original: Finite-dimensional real E of rank n+1, positive natural n; endpoints in S; C1 closed-unit-interval paths; extended nonnegative length distance.
domains.reconstructed: The same E/n/endpoints, EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) sphere model, unitInterval half-space model, lower Lebesgue integral and ENNReal codomain.
domains.evidence: Compiler riemannianEDist_def, Path and unitInterval bodies and the pinned Mathlib interval comparison implement exactly the source path convention.

quantifiers.original: For every eligible E and positive n of the specified rank, every x,y in S; the infimum ranges over every C1 endpoint-constrained path.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universal E/structures, n/rank Fact/hn, then arbitrary x,y; the definition binds Path x y followed by its C1 proof.
quantifiers.evidence: The theorem has no hidden section-variable hypotheses, no distinctness or nonantipodality condition and no preselected path.

assumptions.original: Real inner product, finite dimension, rank n+1 with n>0 and sphere endpoints; speed law, path regularity and integrability are proved internally.
assumptions.reconstructed: Compatible normed additive and real inner-product structures, FiniteDimensional, rank Fact, hn and sphere endpoints; the local ENorm is specified by definition.
assumptions.evidence: Module lines 199-218 fix ENorm inside the conclusion and construct ENormSMulClass inside the proof from linearity. Helper hypotheses are supplied by local proofs; no supplied geodesic, bound or auxiliary measure is a public premise.

conclusion.original: Induced distance is arccos of the ambient real inner product, finite and in [0,pi].
conclusion.reconstructed: riemannianEDist with that exact norm equals ENNReal.ofReal(Real.arccos(inner R x y)).
conclusion.evidence: The angle is nonnegative, so ofReal is a faithful finite encoding. This is not equality with the inherited chord distance.

scopes.original: Global all-pairs pointwise identity, including equal and antipodal endpoints; interior/a.e. derivative identities suffice for length.
scopes.reconstructed: The same global identity, C1 unit-interval path class and nonnegative Lebesgue integral; no a.e. restriction on endpoint pairs.
scopes.evidence: Frame lines 163-170 cover zero residual, interval comparison lines 241,255-259 allows theta=0, and lower-integral lines 280-293 explicitly handle endpoints by restricting to Ioo.

constant_dependencies.original: Unit radius fixes coefficient one, with angle at most pi; no unspecified parameter-dependent constant.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same exact angle, without an extra dimension-, endpoint- or path-dependent factor.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The regularization a and frame u are internal proof variables and do not survive in the theorem conclusion.
